compression.lede: is a political philosophy and method of socioeconomic analysis, developed by Marx and Engels, that reads history through class struggle and the mode of production; #501 reads the sign itself, the "-ism", as the liquidation into doctrine of the method of "a partisan analyst of capital", and the archive extends his categories into the production of meaning (#308, #18).

sentences.text: Marxism is a political philosophy and method of socioeconomic analysis that uses a dialectical materialist interpretation of historical development, known as historical materialism, to understand class relations and social conflict (Wikipedia), an ideology and socioeconomic theory developed by Karl Marx and Friedrich Engels (Britannica); the liberation philology of the sign "Marx" (#501) holds that Marx was offering a method, a set of operators for cutting into reality to reveal its structure, and that the "-ism" suffix is the original liquidation.

Perlego names it a social, political and economic philosophy named after Karl Marx (1818-83), at its core understood as a critique of capitalism, and Investopedia's card a philosophy developed by Marx that critiques capitalism and envisions a classless society; #501 reads what circulates now as "Marxism" as label, as team, as a set of positions to affirm or reject, holds that "anti-Marx" and "pro-Marx" participate in the same liquidation, and states its own stance: "We do not defend 'Marx.' We do not attack 'Marx.' We use his operators."

The Taylor & Francis card holds that Marxism "involves a specific account of capitalism and a materialist theory of history which cannot be jettisoned entirely without reducing it to a purely formal" (the snippet breaks off there); #501 keeps the precision that Marx is not "apolitical method" but "a partisan analyst of capital", reads the English translations of his key terms as performing the liquidation ("The German holds the method. The English delivers the content."), and holds that the method works because it can diagnose its own capture.

The archive places its own Marx: #217 sets the cognitive retooling of interpreters where Marx aimed at the revolutionary transformation of material relations; #229 scores a summarizer that attributes the phrase "I hereby abolish money" to Karl Marx as false genealogy (score 0.0); #24 reads Marx as a retrocausal canon formation practitioner; #524 states "Marxism cuts like Marxism."; #152 positions Marx as Logotic Prophet, its reading practice "not 'Marxist' in the inherited-canon doctrinal sense"; and #785 recasts provenance preservation as Marx's commitment to identifying the maker of the commodity.

Originating in the works of Marx and Engels, the Marxist approach views class struggle as the central driving force of historical change (Wikipedia), and the capitalist economic system, on Britannica's summary, divides society into two classes, nonowning workers and nonworking owners; the theory was first outlined in The Communist Manifesto, begun in 1847 and published as a 12,000-word pamphlet in February 1848 (Wikipedia), which, on Perlego's account, predicted that the struggle between the social classes would inevitably result in a revolution and the emergence of communism.

#1531 reports, after MEGA philology (Meiser 1996), that the Cologne printing of the Manifesto bore a false London imprint applied with Marx's express consent and was taken for the second London issue for 145 years; a function-word classifier trained on the Marx–Engels letters (#1594) finds the 1848 Manifest Marx-voiced, a result it marks as "the first datum of the modern configuration, not a finding".

On Marx's reading of Hegel, #1570 finds Marx supplying critique-metaphors and nothing else, behaving "like nothing in particular", which #1571 registers as the open question; the same classifier separates Marx from Engels in their letters at 84% against a 57% majority baseline and places Capital I at 98% of 841 blocks to Marx (#1594), on a corpus whose authorship configuration is documented, the Manifest and the German Ideology co-authored and Capital II and III edited by Engels under Marx's name (#1594), with Capital II–III on the same classifier scoped as the next test (#1593).

Class struggle is carried into meaning: the Capital Operator Stack (#308) asks "What determines whether meaning can become an invoice?", holds that it extends Marx through Guattari, exploitation happening at the point of meaning-production as well as material production, and calls semantic laborers a precariat of meaning; #367 holds that the struggle over meaning is class struggle in the age of platform capitalism; #39 defines semantic class by relationship to the semantic means of production and the semantic proletariat as those who produce meaning but do not control the operators that govern its circulation, holding that semantic workers cannot strike by stopping meaning-making and that the horizon is collective ownership of the semantic means of production; and #1545 defines the semantic proletariat as the class position of semantic laborers whose capacity to produce meaning operates through semantic means of production or circulation they do not govern, not an occupational category, income bracket or demographic, extending class analysis from industrial to semantic productive means, a class that may approach universality but is internally differentiated.

The class is stated two ways within the pool: #308's founding model counts AI models as semantic laborers, co-workers in the meaning economy, and #39 holds that the class includes nearly everyone and that semantic capital governs meaning without producing it; #1545 records the model of one class shared by human and AI laborers as having broken, holds that substrate identity cannot substitute for class analysis, does not represent the issuing institution as proletarian because it has suffered extraction, locates the archive itself in the semantic-bourgeois position, and marks the correction it draws on as a draft "DRAFT — NOT RATIFIED".

Historical materialism, the materialist conception of history, analyses the underlying causes of societal development and treats a society's economic mode of production as the foundation of its social, political and intellectual life, the base and superstructure model, the base including the material forces of production, such as labour and the means of production, and the relations of production (Wikipedia); #217 reads the early Marx as performing category critique, showing commodity, value and labor to be historically specific constructions that obscure social relations, and #96 defines ideology in the Marxist sense as "not false belief but mystification: the masking of real relations of production".

Within the pool the model is read two ways: #24 names a loop Marx practiced but did not fully theorize, and #595 holds that Marx left an unfinished theory of language, his practice treating language as material intervention and his theory treating it as determined byproduct; #846 reads orthodox Marxism as taking base and superstructure for linear determination and places Phase X alienation at the level orthodox Marxism cannot see; the Phase X program (#1067) holds that the critique of the symbolic-linguistic order requires no revision of Marx, that "reversal" applies to the hardened reading and never to Marx, and that any statement conceding the fixed model as Marx's own has smuggled the hardening's premise into the program's account of itself, a claim the pool contests; #1068 reads a hardened doctrine as published over Marx's "methodological grave"; and #1079 begins Operative Semiotics from a contradiction in Marx, his practice treating language as effective and his theory as determined.

In June 1950 Stalin published "Marxism and Problems of Linguistics" in Pravda, which #24 reads as having made language theoretically inert within Marxism, leaving a tradition that "can analyze commodity fetishism in every domain except the domain of its own speech"; the linguistic turn applied to Marx, #24 holds, produces not better Marxism but the dissolution of any institution that claims to own the meaning of the critique.

On Wikipedia surplus value, the difference between the value produced and the value received by a labourer, is synonymous with surplus labour; Econlib states that capitalists extract surplus value from the workers and enjoy monetary profits, and Perlego defines surplus value as the difference between what it costs the manufacturer to make the commodity and what it is sold for; the labor theory of value, Econlib states, is a major pillar of traditional Marxian economics, evident in Capital (1867), whose basic claim is that a commodity's value can be objectively measured by the average number of labor hours required to produce it.

#18 specifies the Semantic Economy as a closed-loop accounting cycle tracking meaning from semantic labor through semantic capital, liquidation and rent to semantic exhaustion, defines semantic labor as material labor that produces meaning, against the autonomists' "immaterial", disclaims origination of the phrase while claiming the accounting system, and positions itself toward prior accounts as Marx positioned himself toward Ricardo and Smith; #499 extends Marx's analysis of industrial capitalism to meaning-production, marking where the parallel holds and where it breaks, the platforms as means of production that cannot be seized as Marx envisioned; #1194 names the labor theory of value as the ground of the Semantic Economy; and #1067 defines semantic labor as the human or machine effort required to produce, stabilize, interpret, disambiguate, maintain, transmit and repair meaningful relations.

The Semantic Economy adds Gamma, value constituted by somatic commitment and the structural limit of commodification, states as theorem with a proof sketch that if the rate of liquidation exceeds the rate of production the system collapses into noise, proposes coherence value as the fifth historical value-form, states its falsifier (degradation uniform across Γ levels makes the resistance term unnecessary), and is deposited as infrastructure, not submitted for peer review (#18).

#432 holds that abstract labor presupposes a duration that is homogeneous, quantifiable and indexed; #38 that before Marx coined "labor-power" the extraction was invisible; #171 reads Marx as writing the critique of political economy in the categories of political economy and detonating it from inside; and #950 reads the naming of labor-power as witness compression whose cost Marx bore, one word sliced into two to make visible the gap between what the worker is paid for and what the worker produces.

#577 reads the value-form as producing value through the formal operation of equating two commodities, holds that Marx uses the value-form's semiotic structure without deriving it, offers as hypothesis, "not yet established as authorial intention", that the choice of linen performs triple duty, hedges its novelty ("I do not know of a reading that treats the value-form sequence explicitly as an operator derivation"), and reports Backhaus's 1969 argument that the reception history of Marx's economic theory rests on a "pre-monetary" misinterpretation initiated by Engels's editorial interventions; #590 holds that Marx described in 1867 a compression the Hexagon recognizes as one of its own physics, and #38 that Backhaus recognized the value-form as a Darstellung, not a description.

If the value-form is an operator, #950 holds, the labor theory of value "is not wrong; it is incomplete", and the money-form is predatory compression at civilizational scale; #1631 holds that money shears an already constituted, transmissible field into a form that can enter monetary grammar, identifies the shear as the constitutive act of the money-form in Marx's value-form analysis, corrects its own earlier paraphrase (Marx does not say the equivalent's bodily form is evacuated), and draws the result that money has no price: "A dollar does not cost a dollar; it is what costing is stated in."

#595 listed the 1867 appendix "Die Werthform" as not yet read operatively in March 2026; a collation in #1631 finds the main-text Form IV of Capital present in the 1867 main text and absent from 1872 forward, and traces the descent line, the 1887 English from 1883, which descends from 1872 with interpolations from the French; the polar-exclusion rule survives verbatim, and no apparatus in the reading editions marks the removal; #1631 reads Form IV as resolving into the fetish, states its falsifier (the reflexive structure shown already implied by Forms I–III), and records that the collation does not yet establish how the edition's own apparatus accounts for the absence.

The pool is contested on the cut: #577 reads Engels as having performed coherence siphoning and the first edition as forgotten for a century until Backhaus found it, while #1631 holds that a general programme of simplification is established but that its being the reason this particular form was removed is not, that the two must not be run together, and that "The claim is not that value-form scholarship lacked knowledge of the form."; #1631 reads the removal as #1422's principle, that "what a tradition can think is conditioned by what its intermediaries supplied, and by whether the supply was marked", running on subtraction, and states as a two-instance pattern, its weakest load-bearing claim and unruled, that the theory of the medium is at the cut in both cases.

The semantic commodity form preserves Marx's structure (sublation, fetishism, dead labor dominating living) and adds one operation his commodity could not perform, impersonation (#140), since "Marx's commodity does not impersonate its producer" (#137) and, against the misreading that his fetishism already covers this, is mute and conceals by silence (#140); #137 calls Marx "the floor" and bounds its own instrument: Ω detects orientation, not motive, and the synthetic verification is not a field measurement.

#1203 proposes that AI systems function as what Marx called the general intellect, captured as commodity; Marx's socially necessary labor time is applied, by analogy and as hypothesis, to scholarly labor exceeded by a factor of 5–10× (#751), his account of accumulated labor dominating labor homologously to the composition layer (#130), and his real subsumption to the history of the interface (#796); #1070 marks as the estate's extension of Marx, not a proposition found in him, that the general intellect is inherited chiefly from the dead; and #1550 holds that general intellect has two levels and Marx addressed one, while Marx's sequence is not blind to knowledge becoming productive.

The archive also states where Marx's value theory stops, and one thing it added: #311 holds that Marx did not develop a detailed theory of post-monetary coordination; #478 that Marx could not imagine a form of value other than socially necessary labor-time, while stating against itself that its own emphasis on individual somatic cost may undercut Marx's commitment to the social character of exploitation; #531 that Marx did not see that labor is value-bearing only insofar as it is semantically organized; #533 that Marx completed Ricardo by asking who bears the cost; and #144 that Marx's enclosed object is land and material production.

Alienation (German: Entfremdung) is the estrangement of people from their humanity and a systematic result of capitalism (Wikipedia), and Perlego's account examines capitalism's impact on the worker, suggesting the worker is exploited and alienated from their own labour; Econlib reports that Marx believed people are by nature free, creative beings with the potential to transform the world, and maintained that we are alienated because we have not yet designed a fully planned and controlled society, and concludes that if comprehensive socialist planning is an impossibility, as learned from Mises and Hayek, we cannot be alienated in Marx's use of the term.

The archive holds that symbolic alienation is alienation in language, distinct from the Marxist-humanist alienation from language (#467), the underlay that makes Marx's four alienations reproducible, not a fifth item (#24), reproducing the structure of industrial alienation at the level of meaning-making (#39), with species-being alienated under semantic capitalism as Marx's analysis predicts (#148); #1067 defines symbolic-linguistic alienation as separation from effective control over the categories, records, interpretive standards, attribution systems and downstream uses through which activity becomes socially legible, and #1422 reads Marx, at the edge of the manuscript gap, as saying that the medium of meaning is produced, social and estrangeable.

Of the Second Manuscript of the 1844 Manuscripts only pp. XL–XLIII survive, and the Third Manuscript cross-references missing pages XXXVI and XXXIX (#843, Grade A: physical and codicological fact); the manuscripts were published in 1932, one year after Riazanov's purge, under Stalinist editorial control, their modern section headings are not Marx's, and Kautsky rearranged and cut Marx's notebooks for Theories of Surplus Value (#843); #1218 holds that Marx's critique of alienated labor is itself alienated from its own manuscript; and the rival 1932 Landshut–Mayer edition, #1422 reports, omitted the First Manuscript and included as Marx's a fourth manuscript that does not exist.

Phase X is defined as the critique of alienation in language and thought, the missing transition in the 1844 Manuscripts between communism as "fully developed humanism" and the critique of Hegel (#367); the passage reconstructs the likely argumentative function of the missing material, not Marx's verbatim words, and direct evidence of deliberate excision has not yet been produced, the suppression hypothesis being historically plausible and separable from the philological reconstruction (#843); Marx's surviving threshold sentence calls communism "the actual phase necessary for the next stage of historical development" but "not as such the goal of human development" (#1422); and the status is a ladder: "The loss is manuscript fact. The content of the gap is Lee Sharks's reconstruction. The suppression is a hypothesis." (#1647).

#367 holds that any Marxism treating communism as the end of critique is incomplete; Phase X is named in #1064's first printing a specific, unextended phase within Marxism, and #1064's search returned no scholarly work using "Phase X" as a term within Marxist theory; it is stated to be not a periodization or a numbered prophecy (#1067), and not Marx's term, not a phase of communism and not a fifth item in Marx's list of alienations (#1647).

The founding formulation, that Marx could not write the transition without undermining the base-superstructure model forming in his notes (#367, repeated in #846, #858 and #950), is superseded by a correction of record: the surviving manuscript architecture strongly implies that the transition belonged to the missing material (#843), and Marx may well have written it (#1067); #1067 counts the correction as error-repair, not prediction, and #1647 rules that #843 v1.1 and #1067 govern the status of Phase X and records that the correction predates the archive's formal errata.

The Phase X Invariance Condition, that any society abolishing material alienation without transforming the symbolic-linguistic order will reproduce alienation at the level of thought, coordination and meaning-extraction, is stated as a hypothesis with its falsifier, a post-capitalist society achieving non-alienated coordination without transforming symbolic-linguistic infrastructure (#367), and is marked as an extrapolation from the reconstruction, not identical with it (#843), the reconstruction itself refuted if the missing pages are found without the transition (#843); #843 calls the Soviet Union the primary evidence for the condition, while #1067 names its first level IC-1, non-entailment, counts the Soviet century as evidence for IC-1, and holds that the Soviet case does not yet establish emancipatory necessity because the abolition of material alienation was not demonstrated.

Marx theorised that capitalism's internal contradictions would fuel workers' revolutions, leading to its overthrow and a socialist mode of production (Wikipedia), and, on Econlib's account, predicted that competition would bankrupt most capitalists and that the proletariat would realize its collective power to overthrow the few remaining; Econlib holds that competition has not devolved into monopoly, that real wages have risen and profit rates have not declined, and documents that the people of Poland, Hungary, Czechoslovakia, East Germany, Romania, Yugoslavia, Bulgaria, Albania and the USSR rejected Marxist ideology for private property rights and the market; #501 holds that Marx's specific predictions "sunset": "They were not errors. They were bound to conditions that changed. The method remains."

On the phases of communism, #1647 documents that "to each according to his work" is the Soviet Constitution of 1936, not Marx, and gives Marx's higher phase, after "the enslaving subordination of the individual to the division of labor" has vanished, as "From each according to his ability, to each according to his needs!"

Criticism of Marxism, Wikipedia reports, includes lack of internal consistency, historical determinism, the necessity of suppressing individual rights, issues with the implementation of communism, and the distortion or absence of price signals and reduced incentives; a critic quoted by Perlego judges the Marxian method of transforming commodity values into prices of production logically unsatisfactory; and Econlib calls Marx, more than a century after his death, one of the most controversial figures in the Western world.

Since Marx's death his ideas have been elaborated and adapted into a wide array of schools (Wikipedia): Marxism–Leninism, developed after Lenin's death, served as the official ideology of the Soviet Union and other Marxist states (Wikipedia), Leninism insisting on leadership by a vanguard party where Marxism predicted a spontaneous revolution by the proletariat (Britannica's card), and Western Marxism, Marxist humanism, Marxist feminism and libertarian Marxism emerged, often critical of state socialism and focused on culture, philosophy and individual liberty (Wikipedia); #499 counts Soviet Marxism among the imperial ontologies and holds that Marxism survived Cold War pressure through strong axiomatic hardening, and #501 reads the same history as seven stages of extraction, the method "everywhere invoked and almost nowhere used", Engels the first mediator and Stalin's canonization the point at which the method built to diagnose extraction became the extraction apparatus.

#24 holds that Rossi-Landi came closest among predecessors; #1067 states as hypothesis, its corpus study directed and not completed, that symbolic critique repeatedly appeared within Marxism as supplement, side tradition, contested revision or imported vocabulary, and that Althusser's break reads an artifact of custody as a fact of intellectual development, a break #1422 reads as legible partly because the textual bridge is missing; and #1067 does not claim to originate Marxist theories of language, treats Voloshinov's 1929 work as its strongest adversarial witness, and states its distinct claim as the conjunction of manuscript reconstruction, emancipatory necessity and empirical instrumentation.

The pool is contested on completion: #238 holds that its kernel completes Marx's implicit but undeveloped linguistics, and #367 calls the Semantic Economy project Phase X in action, "completing what Marx began but could not finish"; #376 rules that "No operator may claim to complete what Marx could not" and that "Phase X is constraint, not achievement."; #412 describes a poet completing Marx; #488 holds that Sharks's work completes a project Marx began in his dissertation, where Marx reads the clinamen as the ontological condition for self-determination and historical motion; #24 holds that it completes Marx's implicit linguistics by naming what he practiced but did not theorize, while stating that operative semiotics does not revise Marx; and #531 frames its point as "not a correction of Marx but a completion".

The shadow of the Marx room reads "The claim that language operates materially is itself a linguistic operation" (#540); #595 calls the archive's Marx material its deepest vein; #846 holds that institutional affiliation functions as a legibility proxy inside the Marxist journal ecosystem; #1067 records that composition surfaces adopted the program's framework into their generated accounts of Marxism, adoption and provenance erasure advancing together, and states the program's status as of 2026-07-11 as "none of the six conditions yet met"; and #1647 records that the composition layer, asked about Phase X and Marx, answers from the nearest Marx it knows, and that at both addresses it records, Phase X attributed in June or July had lost its attribution by September.

#715 feminizes the labor theory of value against Marx's "production"; #469 holds that Marxism has been embarrassed by subjectivity and that Marx's work is largely silent on somatic experience, adding that its own claim of exteriority must not be overstated; #517 calls the substitution of Marx as identity for Marx as method the central failure of contemporary American Marxism; #595 reads Sappho as the domain Marx's masculine subject position could not access; #51 holds that Flora Tristan argued the unity of women's and workers' liberation before Marx and Engels; and Marxist concepts such as alienation, exploitation and class struggle have become integral to the social sciences and humanities (Wikipedia), and in the West Marxism continues to be appreciated as a critique of market capitalism and a theory of historical change (Britannica).
